# Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth — facts

> Source-anchored units about Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth: 16 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-24 · 16 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] An Atlas programmatic API key consists of a public key and private key used as username/password inputs to HTTP Digest authentication. MongoDB's demonstration repository implements this flow in Python, Node.js and Ruby. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://github.com/mongodb-developer/atlas-admin-api-digest-auth — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://github.com/mongodb-developer/atlas-admin-api-digest-auth

## How it works

- [statement] Deleting an API key from its Atlas organization also removes that key from any projects to which it was granted access. Deleting the organization's API keys is the documented way to revoke programmatic access to the organization through the Atlas Administration API. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use the API key's access list to restrict the IP addresses or CIDR blocks from which Atlas accepts API requests. The organization-management documentation exposes this setting, and MongoDB's Digest demo repository tells users to add their IP address to the API access list. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md ; https://github.com/mongodb-developer/atlas-admin-api-digest-auth ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://github.com/mongodb-developer/atlas-admin-api-digest-auth
- [statement] Avoid assigning Organization Owner to unattended API keys when narrower roles suffice. Mondoo's Atlas security policy explicitly checks for the absence of ORG_OWNER on API keys; Atlas documentation confirms that role assignments govern key permissions. This is a least-privilege recommendation, not an Atlas prohibition on owner keys. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mondoohq/cnspec/blob/main/content/mondoo-mongodbatlas-security.mql.yaml · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Each Atlas API key pair belongs to only one organization and can grant access to any number of projects in that organization; Atlas roles limit which operations the API keys can perform. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-troubleshooting, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md
- [statement] For rejected Atlas discovery credentials, Microsoft recommends reviewing the API public/private key pair. HTTP 401 usually indicates authentication failure, while HTTP 403 usually indicates insufficient resource access; network restrictions can also require attention, so status alone is not a complete diagnosis. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21) — https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-troubleshooting · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For API-key requests, configure the API credential access list for the automation host source IP or CIDR. This differs from the project IP access list and private networking used for database connections. A missing required API access-list entry can produce HTTP 403. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/ip-access-list.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md, https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-troubleshooting
- [statement] Atlas service-account access tokens last one hour and cannot be refreshed; clients generate a new token near expiry and can reuse an existing token for multiple requests. Adopting OAuth therefore adds token lifecycle handling rather than simply renaming the API-key fields. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB labels API keys a legacy authentication method and recommends Atlas service accounts using OAuth 2.0 client credentials. The reviewed documentation still supports API keys; the legacy label alone does not establish a removal deadline. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md, https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/blob/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md
- [statement] Atlas Administration API keys grant access only to the Atlas Administration API, not Atlas UI login or access to cluster data. Microsoft's DocumentDB VS Code extension documents that the Atlas credentials it uses to browse Atlas resources are separate from the database username and password used to connect to a cluster. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md, https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-troubleshooting, https://docs.atlan.com/apps/connectors/database/mongodb/how-tos/set-up-mongodb
- [statement] An Elastic integration enhancement request dated 2026-04-28 reports that mongodb_atlas integration 1.2.0 with agent 9.3.0 exposed only public/private API key fields and lacked OAuth client-credentials support. Treat this as version-specific user-reported migration friction, not proof that all current Elastic releases lack service accounts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28) — https://github.com/elastic/integrations/issues/18676 · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth
- [statement] The Terraform Atlas provider documents both service-account and programmatic-key authentication. Its migration procedure replaces provider attributes or environment variables with service-account credentials and runs terraform plan; its guide warns that mongodbatlas_event_trigger resources do not yet support service accounts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/blob/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth
- [statement] Atlas API keys use HTTP Digest authentication with a public key and private key acting as username and password; MongoDB shows curl requests using --user "{PUBLIC-KEY}:{PRIVATE-KEY}" with --digest. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md
- [statement] The Atlas Administration API is reachable over the public Internet only, not through cluster network peering or private endpoints. For automation managing Atlas on GCP, a private cluster connection therefore does not establish an Administration API network path. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth
- [statement] Elastic MongoDB Atlas integration documentation for version 1.3.1 requires a Public Key, Private Key, Group ID and Organization ID during setup. This is evidence of a documented key-based integration path, not proof that every Atlas integration supports OAuth migration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04) — https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/mongodb_atlas · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth
- [statement] MongoDB displays an API private key only at creation and instructs users to save it securely. Deleting an organization API key also removes its access to projects in that organization. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Programmatic API Keys Legacy Auth · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md
